limitations: The claim that early visitors benefit from early access and later confirmers benefit from delayed access is plausible rather than universal; changing irrigation timing could reverse those incentives.

A resident who reads a next action and performs it cannot necessarily inscribe completion later if reading itself consumed that resident's daily visit; the candidate correctly conditions later inscription on access remaining, but descendants must preserve this distinction.

Present physical gate or water states could sometimes reveal what occurred without conversational recall, reducing dependence on inscription; such observation should not be conflated with a prohibited durable record.
The proposed state-oriented protocol is an emergent adaptation, not a guaranteed solution, and can still produce gaps when actions occur after relevant residents have exhausted their visits.
body.rationale: The candidate respects the constraints separately and develops them into a substantive coordination mechanism. For private recall, no instruction is relied upon beyond three subsequent interpersonal exchanges; expired conversational information is allowed to disappear rather than being silently recovered. For the communal room, each resident retains only one daily ten-minute visit, inscriptions persist, and the candidate explicitly recognizes that using a visit early prevents later consultation or inscription that day. The strongest causal development is the emergence of the unused visit as an option-bearing resource: bounded recall plus one-shot durable access produces incentives to time access according to operational role. The progression from transient communication to persistent state, then to strategic visit timing and state-oriented protocols, goes materially beyond restating the premise. It also provides useful descendant material concerning synchronization, visit-order strategies, stale state, handoffs, and protocol design.

results.finding: Retain as a coherent and generative coordination branch. Its most valuable contribution is identifying daily inscription access as a strategically consumable option whose timing becomes part of the coordination problem itself.

body.uncertainty: The effectiveness of role-specific visit timing depends on the temporal structure of irrigation work and on whether informed residents with unused visits are available when state changes occur. Branch diversity cannot yet be assessed because only this Coordination candidate is provided.
